children: By Anushree Mukherjee and Vishak Mathew

Gold prices were little changed on Monday ahead of the Federal Reserve's meeting next week, where policymakers are expected to hold interest rates, while lower oil prices limited downside pressure on bullion.
Spot gold
held steady at $4,163.65 per ounce by 9:03 a.m. EDT (1303 GMT). US gold futures
for December delivery were unchanged at $4,183.10 per ounce.

"It is not just about whether the Fed hikes next week or waits until December; the tone of its guidance will matter. A hawkish message could bring further short-term weakness for gold," said Fawad Razaqzada, market analyst at Forex.com.
Investors are also awaiting US Personal Consumption Expenditures data next week, the central bank's preferred gauge of inflation.
According to the CME's FedWatch Tool, traders see an 82.8% chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged this month, while expectations for a December increase remain at 90%.
The Fed has raised interest rates once this year, a quarter-point hike in September.
Meanwhile, the International Monetary Fund expects the European Central Bank to likely raise interest rates by 25 basis points at least one more time this year to fight inflationary pressures.
While gold is typically considered a hedge against inflation, higher interest rates reduce the appeal of the non-yielding asset.
Oil prices slipped from a five-month high on Monday after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs on Russia that may lead to more Russian fuel exports.
The drop in oil prices eased some inflation concerns after strong US CPI and PPI readings last week, driven in part by a surge in gasoline costs.
"In our view, key resistance remains at $4,235, while support continues to emerge below $4,100," said Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank.
Among other metals, spot silver
gained 0.86% to $57.49 per ounce, platinum
rose 0.76% to $1,642.71 per ounce and palladium
climbed 1.57% to $1,129.86 per ounce.
